CONGRANT.SPONORG: Texas Academy of Medicine, Engineering, Science and Technology
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The project aims to develop a federated learning (FL) framework tailored for distributed medical data that preserves privacy while supporting multi-modal integration. It will design efficient aggregation strategies to manage noisy, heterogeneous, and potentially adversarial client updates, and incorporate a large-scale supernet model as a meta-evaluator, leveraging knowledge distillation to improve model performance, fairness, and explanation quality. Ultimately, the project seeks to deliver a scalable and transferable framework that can serve as a model for secure and trustworthy medical AI deployment across diverse healthcare systems.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Enhancing the Security of IoBT Infrastructure with Decentralized Ledger
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Enhancing the Security of IoBT Infrastructure with Decentralized Ledger

PI: Hansheng Lei
Co-PI: Xu Lei, Liyu Zhang, Fitra Khan, Mahmoud Quweider

Motivation and challenges. The Internet of Things (IoT) aims at to build an architecture to integrate a wide variety of devices for computation, sensing, communication, and actuation. This concept is then extended to the Internet of Battlefield Things (IoBT) that can connect all types of units in the battlefield to enable predictive analytics for intelligent command and control and battlefield services. Considering the complexity of IoBT deployment environment, an edge-cloud architecture is a suitable way to connect IoBT devices. Edge computing datacenters are deployed closer to the physical places where IoBT devices are used, and this allows data to be collected and processed locally. IoBT applications running in different edge computing datacenters only need to interact with each other through the cloud datacenter when necessary. Therefore, this architecture greatly reduces unnecessary communication and latency. Furthermore, the edge-cloud paradigm is also consistent with the design of 5G network, which is believed to be critical for DoD. Systems built on top of an IoBT infrastructure, especially systems involving AI, rely on data collected by IoBT for making support decisions and conducting operations of critical infrastructure. A failure of preserving the integrity of such a system can cause serious consequences. However, there is a lack of end-to-end protection of IoBT and systems built on top of it, especially AI systems, which prevents fully unleashing the potential of IoBT.
The goal. The goal of the proposed efforts is to provide end-to-end protection of key IoBT applications, which is achieved through the following objectives: (i) A novel blockchain architecture that is designed to work with IoBT and able to handle a large number of IoT devices in an efficient manner; (ii) an end-to-end IoBT infrastructure protection mechanism based on the newly proposed blockchain architecture, especially for AI systems built on top of it; and (iii) a prototype implementation of the proposed framework and a testbed environment for benchmarking.
Technical approach. The proposed blockchain based end-to-end IoBT protection solution consists of two major components: (i) A novel blockchain scheme that is integrated with edge-cloud architecture and able to support a large number of IoBT devices; and (ii) an integration of the protection mechanism into the proposed blockchain scheme to guarantee the effectiveness of IoBT applications running in the edge-cloud environment. The novel blockchain scheme consists of multiple edge-blockchains and one cloud-blockchain, where multiple edge-blockchains can support massive number of IoBT devices, and the new protocols proposed herein allow each of the blockchains to verify information stored on other blockchains in an efficient way. This novel blockchain scheme is then leveraged to protect AI systems through two steps: protecting the data collection procedure and protecting the model building procedure, which is usually expensive and hard to verify. Due to the immutability feature of blockchain and our novel stochastic checking mechanism, an adversary cannot compromise the integrity of an AI system without tampering with the majority of the peers of the proposed blockchain system.
Expected results. The expected results of the proposed efforts are three-fold: (i) The design and implementation of the edge-cloud blockchain and integrated protection mechanism for IoBT applications, especially AI related applications; (ii) a testbed to benchmark the developed system and future systems such as distributed asynchronous processing and analysis of things; and (iii) involving undergraduate and graduate students in research and development in IoT and IoBT areas.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Center for Army HBCU/MI Research Centers of Excellence: Decentralized Ledger based Forensics Infrastructure
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: 1 Motivation and ChallengesThe proposed research targets 1. Information Science, b. Research Area 2 DigitalForensics.Effective information collection, processing, and utilization play an increasingly important role ina variety of defense applications. As a result, the deployment of information systems becomesubiquitous. While the rich data that is unavailable in the past brings many benefits, it also createsnew challenges for forensics. For instance, it is hard to process the massive data to extractdigital evidence manually, and the complexity of the system brings a larger attack surface to theadversaries.The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) sheds light on the challenges and many successfulapplications have been developed. However, AI is a doubleedgedsword for digital forensics, i.e.,it has also been proved to be a powerful tool to generate fake evidence. Although new methods arealso proposed to combat AIgeneratedfake evidence, the situation is more like a catandmousegame. Furthermore, AIbasedforensics tools also suffer from all types of attacks such as datapoisoning and model poisoning, which can lead the tools to make wrong conclusions. Therefore,there is an urgent need to address these limitations to fully unleash the potential of AI in digitalforensics.2 The GoalThe goal of the decentralized ledger based forensics infrastructure is to protect the authenticity ofdigital evidence collected from different resources and offer the capability of tracing back whenan issue is detected. Instead of focusing on content analysis to detect/prevent malicious digital evidence,the team plans to adopt a different strategy to address the challenge of preserving the authenticityof digital evidence. Specifically, the team will design and develop a forensics infrastructurethat can provide a complete history of the lifecycle of digital evidence and offer the capability totrace back. From the original data collection to intermediate processing results and the final digitalevidence used for decision making, each step is authenticated and recorded in the system. Toachieve this goal, the proposed system should provide the following features: (i) Irreversible evidencerecording. When a record of digital evidence is added to the system, it cannot be removedor modified. (ii) Scalability. Considering the large number of data sources, the system must bescalable to handle all of them in an efficient manner. (iii) Flexible data authentication. Whilearbitrary data manipulation should be prevented, there are also legitimate operations that can be appliedto collected digital evidence (e.g., figure enhancement). Therefore, the system should allowthese operations without compromising the data authentication protection mechanism. (iv) Highresilience. The system will be deployed in a complex and hostile environment so it needs to beresilient against adaptive adversaries, and offer functionalities such as critical information leakagedetection and fault tolerance. (v) Privacy preserving auditing. A third party may occasionally needto check the correctness of digital evidence records managed by the system, but it does not need toknow the contents of the evidence.

CONGRANT.TITLE: TRUSTVILLE: Teaching and Research Utilizing Security Track based on Versatile Integrated Lab for Learning Enrichment
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Getting students’ interest piqued in a college degree in a STEM field is challenging. However, due to ever increasing pace of technology transformation, the area of computer science is frequently afforded an opportunity to attract students to relatively new areas with visible impact on everyday life and business. Cyber security, a field pervasively touching almost every aspect of modern life, boasts a promise of job growth of 28% from 2016 through 2026 according to BLS. On the other hand, according to ISACA, 84% of organizations believe that only half or fewer of the applicants for security jobs are qualified. This proposal is for enhancing Teaching and Research Utilizing Security Track based on a Versatile Integrated Lab for Learning Enrichment (TRUSTVILLE). The proposed integrated security lab, which includes Internet of Things (IOT) equipment as well, will be familiarizing students with the state of the art cyber security appliances and software in a realistic environment to give them a competitive edge in the job market for serving to fill the existing gap in cyber security in public and private sectors.

The Computer Science Department at The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley has been offering courses in cyber security area, however, a formal cyber security track with the required training has not been offered due to lack of hardware and software. The institution has Data, Intelligence and Security (DIS) group, with its own lab space, and prides itself for hosting the first International Conference on Data, Intelligence and Security (ICDIS) in April 2018. Given the current faculty expertise in cyber security, experience in teaching related courses, having a DIS group with its own lab space and the market potential for cyber security jobs, the university is strategically poised for offering a specialized track in cyber security to enhance teaching and research.

Due to the market demand, the hardware and software related with cyber security are expensive, and this proposal is for securing funds to assist the institution’s ongoing efforts to establish a market driven cyber security track supported by a modern cyber security integrated laboratory. Since low traffic volume is encountered in a lab environment, expensive high-performance ASIC based hardware is not needed. However, the updates to the firmware and software of security hardware, and to the software itself could be as frequent as daily, for example, to block vulnerabilities including zero-day worms. Therefore, most of the expense of cyber security integrated lab is not in the hardware, but rather in the annual subscription of the software to keep the lab current.

The cyber security track in computer science will consist of seven computer science courses geared towards cyber security, three criminal justice courses, and a senior cornerstone project in the area of cyber security. All of these courses will incorporate Project Based Learning (PBL) methodology to familiarize the students with industry grade cyber security tools and appliances. The required integrated laboratory will consist of a gamut of cyber security related hardware and software to understand and analyze the weaknesses of systems and procedures and learn how to strengthen security at different levels. The integrated security laboratory will consist of software and hardware such as IoT devices, IPS, IDS, threat hunting, vulnerability management, traffic monitoring, penetration testing, forensics, encryption, network security and endpoint security for both on premise and cloud assets.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Computational Studies of Snake Venom
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Snake venoms are complex mixtures of toxins. Most major venom toxins have been characterized and their transcripts have been identified from many different snake species. However, the toxin-toxin interactions in the venom remain poorly understood. Therefore, the goal of this proposed project is to decipher the venom complexity by using Crotalus atrox venom as a model system. We will integrate biochemistry and computational approaches to detect the toxin-toxin interactions and simulate the three-dimensional structures of toxin interactions. The expected results will advance our knowledge about how venom toxins assemble into venom complex units to synergistically strengthen their toxic activity.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Promoting Postbaccalaureate Opportunities for Hispanic Americans (PPOHA) Program
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The University of Texas at Brownsville and Texas Southmost College (UTB/TSC) is a public four-year
university that serves more than 17,000 students, over 90 percent of whom are Hispanic coming from the
Rio Grande Valley (RGV) region in south Texas. While Rio Grande Valley is a region of tremendous
potential for growth in terms of human capital (the first in the nation) and in terms of contributions this
population can make to the state and the nation, such potential cannot be realized without the intellectual
and educational resources that have been historically lacking. The region is still plagued with a dismaying
poverty rate of 36.5 percent in 2008. There is an extremely urgent need in Rio Grande Valley to provide
affordable postsecondary education, and produce high-quality graduates with promising employability, in
order to bring radical changes to the local economy.
To respond to such severe regional situations as well as the national imperative to promote postsecondary
education for Hispanic Americans, The University of Texas at Brownsville and Texas Southmost College
proposes a project to improve its graduate programs in computer science (CS) and math as an effort to
expand postbaccalaureate educational opportunities for Hispanic Americans and contribute to the
bootstrapping of regional economy. The project aims to (1) improve the retention and graduation rates of
Hispanic and low-income graduate students in computer science and math; (2) improve the employability
including the ability for Ph.D. study of Hispanic and low-income students upon their graduations; (3)
attract more Hispanic and disadvantaged students to enter into Science, Technology, Engineering, and
Mathematics fields.
Over the life of the grant, the project will integrate proven best practices including: (1) course
development consisting of online course development to facilitate convenient access to these courses and
improve students’ retention rate, and new course development and course redesign in emerging areas such
as bioinformatics, cyber security and distance education in mathematics that will greatly benefit students’
future employment and/or further academic careers; (2) faculty mentored research to engage students in
research and keep them motivated and focused on their graduate study to prompt success; (3) high-school
outreach and teaching activities to build linkages among computer science or math students towards
teaching in high schools and motivate them to pursue a teaching career, as well as to attract more high
school teachers/students to pursue computer science and math undergraduate/graduate degrees; (4)
summer internship program to enable students to get first-hand industry experience through internships
and to be more employable upon graduation; (5) invited speaker series where successful minority
students, scholars and industry leaders will be invited as role models to the University of Texas at
Brownsville and Texas Southmost College to have dialogues with our participating students to inspire
them to pursue advanced study in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics; (6) teaming
graduate students with undergraduate students in research project as well as in regular academic life
through “buddy-mentoring” in order to not only develop the leaderships of graduate students but also
engage undergraduate students to strengthen and widen the pipeline in computer science and math
through graduate degrees.
Upon successful execution of the project, we anticipate the project outcomes to be significant increases in
enrollment, retention and graduate rates, as well as immediate employment rates in the computer science
and math graduate programs. We also anticipate an increased portion of our graduates to go on to pursue
Ph.D. degrees

CONGRANT.TITLE: DURIP:    Build a wind-riding small drone with morphing wings for multi-agent collaborative learning
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
We propose a solution to kill two birds with one stone: develop a morphing wing for drones to ride winds and save battery life. We will mimic bat wings to achieve desired aerodynamic performance through a simple, light, and easy-to-maneuver mechanical design; artificial muscle fibers will replace traditional motors for actuation.  We vision that the drone can extend its wings to glide like a bird when wind is favorable. When wind is not favorable, the wings will be stretched in. With increased flight time, small drones are suitable for real world applications. 
Furthermore, we propose to enable the intelligence of drones by developing algorithms in computer vision, target recognition and multi-agent collaborative learning. Our goal is to explore the low space (<400m altitude) where we see countless applications directly benefiting human life: photography, transportation, surveillance, etc.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Smart Glasses-based solutions for helping people with disabilities is a rather untapped research area. However, it carries tremendous potential to allow a degree of alleviation of the various challenges faced by people with disabilities (PWD). The paper proposes a smart glasses-based research project for people with memory loss conditions, enabling them to create and maintain grocery shopping lists. The goal is to develop a more multifaceted purpose small IoT system. In the proposed project, the design assists users with memory or visual disabilities in creating a grocery shopping list, based on what goods exist in the user’s pantry. The centerpiece of this design is the Raspberry Pi 4B computer, which is a low-cost device. The proposed system architecture allows a referencing image data from pre-built smart glasses, or a camera module embedded in the system, into a user interface application for which the image data is fed into trained image classification models. The resultant output image classification is obtained, which is referenced from the application and displayed as a list in the UI for the user to verify. Once the user verifies groceries, a new list is dynamically created and saved locally, which is referenced into another page in the program for the user to view the list creation data. Ultimately, the work can be expanded to allow a full e-commerce experience. The proposed system allows to compare different machine-learning models for the recognition for grocery items. It also demonstrates a proof-of-concept for assistive smart glasses for people with memory loss conditions, and a variety of future works and developments can be derived from this research.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A Deep Dive into FAT-32 Windows File System: A Digital Forensics Perspective
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: The 5th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Abstract— For digital forensics analysts, the file system of a digital computing/storage device is a great source of relevant information that can aid in an investigation or analysis of a case at hand. Therefore, a solid understanding of the file system details and how to identify, extract, analyze, and present the data on a given device becomes crucial to a successful inquiry or investigation. In this paper, we present a detailed overview of the Windows operating systems FAT-32 file system with an emphasis on its importance from a digital forensics perspective. We review the overall technical mechanisms and processes with context and background by which files are organized including data (content) and metadata/attributes, identify fields that are unique to the file system, point out places where data can be hidden or masked, and how data recovery and carving techniques work with the file system. We also conduct a detailed walk through of each filesystem component using low level tools and verify the results with the current major tools of acquisition, recovery and carving of data.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Glaer et al. (SIAMJCOMP 2009 and TCS 2009) proved that NP-complete languages are polynomial-time mitotic for the many-one reduction, meaning that each NP-complete language L can be split into two NP-complete languages L intersect S and L \ S, where S is a language in P. It follows that every NP-complete language can be partitioned into an arbitrary nite number of NP-complete languages. We strengthen and generalize this result by showing that every NP- complete language can be partitioned into innitely many NP-complete languages. INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Abstract— Critical infrastructure networks can be represented as directed graphs in which nodes represent operation entities and arcs denote dependencies between entities. An informed attacker who wishes to harm the system would aim to use the minimum amount of effort, cost, or resources to produce the maximum amount of damage. Therefore, the most rational strategy would be to attack the most critical nodes of the infrastructure network. Conversely, the system’s operator could work to minimize potential damage if they are able to defend these critical nodes. Thus, it is important for both the attacker and defender to identify which nodes are most important to the network. However, this is a complex optimization problem. This paper presents the problem formulation and corresponding solution for computing the optimal cost attack that takes failure propagation into account. Given a graph representing one or multiple interconnected infrastructures and the attack cost of each node, the proposed method computes the optimal attack that a rational attacker is likely to make. Our problem model can simulate one of two goals: maximizing the damage for a given attack budget or minimizing the cost for a given amount of damage. Our technique relies on integer-linear programming to obtain the solution, given our objective function and sets of constraints for each of the specified goals. As shown by the experimental results, using a wide range of graphs, the proposed solution is very fast in terms of the runtime complexity.

Keywords— Security, Critical Infrastructures, Optimization, Graph Analysis

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Recommender systems are widely used in a variety of scenarios, including online shopping, social network, and contents distribution. As users rely more on recommender systems for information retrieval, they also become attractive targets for cyber-attacks. The high-level idea of attacking a recommender system is straightforward. An adversary selects a strategy to inject manipulated data into the database of the recommender system to influence the recommendation results, which is also known as a profile injection attack. Most existing works treat attacking and protection in a static manner, i.e., they only consider the adversary’s behavior when analyzing the influence without considering normal users’ activities. However, most recommender systems have a large number of normal users who also add data to the database, the effects of which are largely ignored when considering the protection of a recommender system. We take normal users’ contributions into consideration and analyze popular attacks against a recommender system. We also propose a general protection framework under this dynamic setting.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Weak Mitoticity of Bounded Disjunctive and Conjunctive Truth-table Autoreducible Sets
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Theoretical Computer Science
INTELLCONT.CONTRACT_NUM: Research supported in part by NSF CCF grant 1218093
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Glaßer et al. (SIAMJCOMP 2008 and TCS 2009)2 proved existence of two sparse sets A and B in EXP, where A is 3-tt (truth-table) polynomial-time autoreducible but not weakly polynomial-time Turing mitotic and B is polynomial-time 2-tt autoreducible but not weakly polynomial-time 2-tt mitotic. We unify and strengthen both of those results by showing that there is a sparse set in EXP that is polynomial-time 2-tt autoreducible but not even weakly polynomial-time Turing mitotic. All these results indicate that polynomial-time autoreducibilities in general do not imply polynomial-time mitoticity at all with the only exceptions of the many-one and 1-tt reductions. On the other hand, however, we proved that every autoreducible set for the polynomial-time bounded disjunctive or conjunctive tt reductions is weakly mitotic for the polynomial-time tt reduction that makes logarithmically many queries only. This shows that autoreducible sets for reductions making more than one query could still be mitotic in some way if they possess certain special properties.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Abstract— With the advent of cloud computing, the Internet of Things (IoT), and mobile computing, CS faculty are continuously revamping the curriculum material to address such burgeoning set of technologies in practical and relatable ways. Raspberry Pi (RPi) devices represent an ideal hardware/software framework that embodies all these technologies through its simple architecture, small form factor (that minimizes the volume and footprint of a desktop computer), and ability to integrate various sensors and actuators that network together and connect to the Cloud. Therefore, one of the strategies of Computer Science Department, to enhance depth of learning concepts, has been to infuse Raspberry Pi (RPi) in computer science courses. RPi has been incorporated since 2017 in targeted courses, notably, Computer Organization & Assembly Language, Computer Architecture, Database Management Design & Implementation, Unix/Linux Programming, Internet Programming, and Senior Project. An inexpensive credit card sized computer, an RPi lends itself to allow depth of learning of concepts. From implementing firewalls,intrusion detection systems, scripting, client-server based computing, distributed computing, to interfacing with sensors and actuators, a student is guided to polish concepts taught in a class through RPi Project Based Learning (RPBL). Computer science curriculum already provides breadth of learning. The infusion of RPi in key courses provides depth in targeted concepts. There are peripheral desirable consequences as well, including a student learning prevalently used Linux environment even though a targeted course may have nothing directly to do with Linux.Furthermore, RPi provides an opportunity for students to realize that software programs can be interfaced with sensors and actuators to provide immersed experience in programming. From simply interfacing a switch and a Light Emitting Diode (LED) to getting data from sensors,buffering, and uploading to the cloud, a student already would have touched upon multiple disciplines in computer science. This paper provides a blueprint to infusing RPi in the targeted courses, and how each RPi based project provides depth to a targeted concept.

Index Terms—Raspberry Pi, Cloud Computing, Internet of Things (IoT), Mobile Computing, Linux.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
To create an emerging teaching and research institution, a regional university was created that
spans multiple campuses located over an area of hundred miles across the Rio Grande Valley by
merging at least three current institutions. The merge allowed the university to pool its human
and technical resources. Students can now pursue new degrees that were not available before at
one campus or another, take newly available technical or specialty courses, and even select their
own preferred professor when a course is offered by many faculty.
In order to serve students at multiple campuses that are geographically far apart, the university
instituted policies to facilitate accessibility of courses to all students while meeting prerequisites
and minimum enrollment requirements. This paper chronicles the policies, procedures, and
faculty and staff efforts in creating a sustainable framework for implementing a distributed
campus course delivery that is acceptable by the university/college administration, the
department, the faculty, and most importantly the students. Our experience shows that a
successful framework should address many issues, including: Logistics, Scheduling, Faculty
incentives, IT support, course management system and delivery methods, assessment and student
participation. The paper will present our efforts in each of the above areas, showing that despite
the challenges faced, a distributed delivery system can be successful when the above
issues/factors are adequately addressed. The results from our courses at the graduate and
undergraduate levels show that student assessments don’t show any significant difference across
campuses or based on where the home campus of the faculty is. By presenting our study, we
hope that other institutions who are considering distributed education can benefit from our
experience by adopting best practices while avoiding pitfalls.

Abstract— Image retrieval systems have been an active area of research for more than thirty years progressively producing improved algorithms that improve performance metrics, operate in different
domains, take advantage of different features extracted from the images to be retrieved, and have different desirable invariance properties. With the ever-growing visual databases of images and videos produced by a myriad of devices comes the challenge of selecting effective features and performing fast retrieval on such databases. In this paper, we incorporate Fourier descriptors (FD) along
with a metric-based balanced indexing tree as a viable solution to DHS (Department of Homeland Security) needs to for quick identification and retrieval of weapon images. The FDs allow a simple but effective
outline feature representation of an object, while the M-tree provide a dynamic, fast, and balanced search over such features. Motivated by looking for applications of interest to DHS, we have created a basic guns and rifles databases that can be used to identify weapons in images and videos extracted from media sources. speed.

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: There are different traditional approaches to handling a large number of computers or workstations in a campus setting, ranging from imaging to virtualized environments. The common factor among the traditional approaches is to have a user workstation with a local hard drive (nonvolatile storage), scratchpad volatile memory, a CPU (Central Processing Unit) and connectivity to access resources on the network. This paper presents the use of block streaming, normally used for storage, to serve operating system and applications on-demand over the network to a workstation, also referred to as a client, a client computer, or a client workstation. In order to avoid per seat licensing, an Open Source solution is used, and in order to minimize the field maintenance and meet security privacy constraints, a workstation need not have a permanent storage such as a hard disk drive. A complete blue print, based on performance analyses, is provided to determine the type of network architecture, servers, workstations per server, and minimum workstation configuration, suitable for supporting such a solution. INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Pattern Recognition Letters
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: A large number of features have been proposed by researchers for on-line signature verification. However, little work has been done in measuring the consistency and discriminative power of these features. This paper presents a comparative study of features commonly used in on-line signature verification. A consistency model is developed by generalizing the existing feature-based measure to distance-based measure. Experimental results show that the simple features like X-, Y-coordinates, the speed of writing and the angle with the X-axis are amongst the most consistent.

PRESENT.TITLE: Mining Dependent Patterns
PRESENT.ABSTRACT: Association Rule (AR) mining has been studied intensively for the past two decades. Essentially, AR models the conditional probabilities of itemsets. However, AR mining generates an overwhelming number of rules which limits its capability in mining real nuggets. We re-examined the problem and propose to start mining on dependent relationships instead of conditional relationships. In contrast to AR mining, dependence mining has received much less attention in the literature. Here a new model, Dependent Pattern (DP) mining is presented. DP has a solid base in classical statistics and at the same time is suitable for large scale computation with the property of downward closure. We validate the model from different perspectives using a variety of datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that DP has remarkable advantages over AR mining and other related methods. This work serves as a proof of concept. Future work will focus on the theoretical analysis of DP’s scalability.
